cases.AS-001: Confirmed in the text: 'I judged that she would find him there at her coming home: which she did'; and of the trine day, 'therefore I judged that she should see him at that time: which she did.' cases.AS-002: Confirmed in the text: 'And so to this day he hath [attained it by labour]'; 'He has since had a good fortune with his wife, money, and land, and been very successful in trade'.
cases.AS-003: Confirmed in detail in the text: the bargain was struck on 25 April following (the day Venus and the Sun came to their aspect); on 17 May he paid the £530 and his conveyance was sealed — 'six weeks and some days from the time of the Question'; a friend lent him £500 twelve days after (when Mercury turned direct). Lilly adds he did himself injury in money by the bargain but never repented it.
cases.AS-004: Not stated as a postscript in the excerpt, but a matter of historical record: Cambridge was never taken by the King during the Civil War (it remained a Parliamentarian stronghold, headquarters of the Eastern Association). Marked as externally verified, not Lilly-stated.
cases.AS-005: Confirmed in the text: '(It proved that she was in a harbour in the west)' and of the news, '(And so it proved.)'
cases.AS-007: Confirmed in the text: 'It appeared, by a letter from the army on that same Friday, that our generals took on the previous day 120 commanders and gentlemen, 560 common soldiers, and much ammunition.' (Historically: the Battle of Cheriton, 29 March 1644, was a Parliamentarian victory.)
cases.AS-008: Confirmed in the text: 'The Town was delivered for the Parliament's use the 27th of April... three days after the time limited by me was expired; but the very Monday before, being eight days after the Figure set, they began to treat.' Lilly adds the King's relief was beaten back at Caversham Bridge, the Governor (Aston) was hurt in the head (as Saturn in Pisces(?) afflicted by Mars denoted), and they did not want ammunition, as Venus in the 5th signified. See the year flag in inputs (1643 historically; OCR prints 1644).
cases.AS-009: Confirmed in the text: a gentleman of the querent's acquaintance, coming by accident to see a friend in Long Acre, found the dog tied up under a table, knew it to be the querent's, and sent it home that same Monday about ten in the morning — 'to my very great credit.'
cases.AS-010: Confirmed in the 1852 edition's wording: 'Upon the Friday following he came home, and said he had been at Kingston upon Thames; which if true, then he was full West, or a little to the South, and near a great Water, viz. the Thames.'
cases.AS-011: Confirmed in the text: 'My counsel was followed, and the issue was thus: By the Gentleman's means and procurement, the matter was brought on again, the Match effected, and all within twenty days following, to the content of the sorrowful (but as to me unthankful) Lady.'
cases.AS-012: Confirmed in the text: the parson 'being covetous would proceed further... and when he thought to have the matter absolutely on his side, behold, a scurvy Letter, revealing some manifest truths concerning a Female, dashed the good Man's hopes' — he never discovered which neighbour had affronted him.
cases.AS-013: Confirmed in the text: Lilly took out a warrant, kept it private until Sunday 18th, searched only that one house, and 'found part of my fish in water, part eaten, part not consumed; all confessed' — including seven Portugal onions the thief's wife had unknowingly made into pottage.
cases.AS-014: Confirmed in the text: 'The event proved me right, both as to the person and the return of the money, which was within three days after' — although the querent at first 'believed not one word I said.'
cases.AS-015: Confirmed in the text: 'in truth she died the eighth of October, upon which day Mars and [the other significator] were in the eighth degree...'.

cases.AS-205: Of the disease: 'all which was true'; of the event: 'The sick dyed the 28th of July following' — twelve days after the figure of 16 July 1645.

cases.BQ-010: 「果应不成」——其讼终未成（讼事无成）。
cases.BQ-011: 「果被妇人执罪」——周焚松果被一妇人告发/执罪。
cases.BQ-012: 「果应不来，但被日带父爻六害，乃受风雨淋漓之苦也」——倭寇果未至，唯占者遭风雨淋漓之苦。
cases.BQ-014: 「果当日辰时止息」——飓风果于当日辰时停息。
cases.BQ-015: 「其年果应风雨连月，水溢田中，五谷淹腐殆尽也」——其年风雨连月、田中水溢、五谷淹腐殆尽。
cases.BQ-016: 「其年果应倭贼大乱……所以其年劫、烧、杀、伤不可胜计」——其年倭贼大乱，劫掠、焚烧、杀伤不可胜计。
cases.BQ-017: 「果被妇人引祸及已」——其人果然因妇人招致祸事及身。
cases.BQ-019: 「已而果然」——后来果如注家所戒：祸非倭寇、乃官兵之祸。
cases.BQ-020: 「果被获去一第一子……所以子死非命，而弟得回来也」——长子果被掳去且死于非命，弟得归来，占者本人无事。
cases.BQ-021: 「后将插莳，果为阴人少财而去，逾三四日，而天则亢旱难用矣」——插莳之时果因（雇工/阴人）少财而去，逾三四日天大旱至于难用。
cases.BQ-022: 「自始至终，凡遇耘耕收获，辄遇雨，未尝得快作几日也」——全季每逢耘耕、收获皆遇雨，几乎没有痛快作活的日子。
cases.BQ-023: 「至正月，果被原主回赎」——至正月，其田果被原主赎回。
cases.BQ-024: 「果应不死，后因夜啼而妻病作」——鸡果不死，后因鸡夜啼而占者之妻病作。
cases.BQ-025: 「未半日，群蜂满身攒聚，惊惶无措」——占后不到半日，群蜂满身攒聚，占者惊惶无措。
